draft.title: How science corrects itself
card: Scientific knowledge can change when new evidence appears. Scientists treat ideas as the best explanation so far, not as final truth.
Before a study is published, other experts check its methods and conclusions. They can spot errors, gaps or claims the data does not support.
Other scientists run the same test to see if they get the same result. A result that cannot be repeated is doubted.
New evidence can refine or replace an idea. Evidence that the universe is expanding built up over decades, from many observations by many scientists.
draft.remember: Checking by others and new evidence let science find mistakes and improve its ideas.

a.q: Why does a scientist's published result get checked by other scientists who repeat the experiment?
opts: To see whether the same result appears again
To make sure the first scientist gets the credit
To prove that the original idea must be correct
To stop anyone from testing the idea further
a.why: If others get the same result, confidence in it grows. If they do not, a mistake may be found. Repeating a test does not prove an idea must be correct, because later evidence can still change it.
a.clue: Think about what a different result would reveal.

b.q: Dr Lee's team reports that a new fertiliser doubles crop growth. Three other labs repeat the test and see no change. What is the best conclusion?
opts: The first result is doubtful and needs rechecking
The first result is right because it was published first
The other labs must have made the errors, not Dr Lee
Fertiliser tests cannot give reliable results at all
b.why: A result that others cannot repeat is doubted, so the first study needs rechecking for errors. Being first does not make a result right. Failed repeats do not show all fertiliser tests are unreliable.
b.clue: What does the card say about a result that cannot be repeated?

a.best: To see whether the same result appears again

b.best: The first result is doubtful and needs rechecking

proposal.title: How science corrects itself
card: Scientific knowledge can change when new evidence appears. Scientists treat ideas as the best explanation so far, not as final truth.
Before a study is published, other experts check its methods and conclusions. They can spot errors, gaps or claims the data does not support.
Other scientists run the same test to see if they get the same result. A result that cannot be repeated is doubted.
New evidence can refine or replace an idea. Evidence that the universe is expanding built up over decades, from many observations by many scientists.
proposal.remember: Checking by others and new evidence let science find mistakes and improve its ideas.

a.q: Why do other scientists repeat an experiment after its result is published?
opts: To see whether they get the same result
To make sure the first scientist gets the credit
To turn the original idea into a final truth
To check the study before a journal prints it
a.why: Repeating a test shows whether the result holds up. If others get the same result, confidence grows, and if not, a mistake may be found. Checking a study before a journal prints it is peer review, which happens before publication, not after.
a.clue: Think about what a different result would reveal.

b.q: Dr Lee's team reports that a new fertiliser doubles crop growth. Three other labs repeat the test and see no change. What is the best conclusion?
opts: Dr Lee's result is doubtful and needs rechecking
Dr Lee's result stands because it was published first
The three other labs likely made errors, not Dr Lee
Passing peer review showed Dr Lee's result is correct
b.why: A result that others cannot repeat is doubted, so Dr Lee's study needs rechecking for errors. Peer review can spot problems, but passing it does not make a result correct, and later tests can still challenge it.
b.clue: What happens to a result that others cannot repeat?
